items.prose: Inspection under crossed polarizing filters revealed dense magenta and cyan isochromatic fringes around the neck weld of five-liter boiling flasks. The high residual stress (45 nm/cm) requires re-soaking to prevent spontaneous explosive fracture during heating.

Thermocouple calibration drift allowed the lehr to cool through the 510°C glass transformation range at 15°C per minute instead of the required 1.5°C. Permanent tensile stress froze into the wall center, causing twelve boiler sight tubes to snap under finger pressure.

Air-cooling the massive three-quarter-inch thick base of a 20-liter acid carboy created extreme Prince Rupert drop stresses. When a worker set the vessel down on a tiny sand pebble, the localized shock released the tension, detonating the jug into glass dust.

Sealing heavy tungsten electrical leads through Nonex glass envelopes required precise temperature holding at 580°C. Careful annealing eliminated radial compressive stresses, preventing microscopic air leakage along the metal-glass boundary.

Joining pure fused quartz (CTE 5.5x10^-7) to borosilicate glass (CTE 33x10^-7) was achieved via five intermediate glass rings of stepping thermal expansion. Lehr annealing at 610°C for six hours produced an ultra-low retardance (8 nm/cm) leak-tight union.

A seventy-two-hour ultra-slow fine annealing cycle from 540°C down to 350°C relaxed optical anisotropy across four-inch borosilicate prism blanks. Residual retardance dropped below 3 nm/cm, ensuring zero double-refraction distortion in spectrometer optics.

Cold air drafting through an unsealed inspection port chilled the left side of the conveyor belt. The uneven cooling warped forty precision 1,000ml graduated cylinders into banana-like curves, rendering volumetric measurement graduations invalid.
